about: Guided question bank for the scene analysis call. scene_types decides which questions each scene type may use. The AI adapts the wording of question and options to the photo, but cannot add a question that is not listed here. Checked by question_bank.py on every load. By convention the last option is the skip or do-it-differently choice. focal_suggestion is not chosen by the AI: the app asks it once for each focal area the sketcher did not mark, pointing at it with a reticle, filling in $label and $reason from the scene analysis. Its first option adds the area to the plan as a mark along its outline (source 'prompted', design doc item 17). The others are only recorded: one for an area the sketcher already had in mind, one for declining. Each option is a label plus an optional action. An action names an overlay the app shows when the sketcher picks that option; the valid names and what each shows are listed in 'actions'. style_actions swaps an action for one style, e.g. realistic shows the square grid wherever the rule-of-thirds grid would show.

actions.proportions: Proportion check: one unit the AI traced (e.g. a column's height) and 2-3 spans measured against it, e.g. 'roof width = 3.5 units'.
actions.perspective: Eye level and vanishing points, each traced edge extended to its point.
actions.focal_shapes: The AI's traced outlines of the strongest focal areas.
actions.value_study: The photo simplified into a few flat value shapes, light to dark.
actions.rule_of_thirds: The rule-of-thirds grid over the frame.
actions.grid: A square grid for the grid method, cells set by --grid-cell-mm in index.css (10 mm).
actions.describe: Not an overlay: the app shows a short text field so the sketcher can answer in their own words.

focal_suggestion.question: There is the $label here. $reason Add it to your plan?

mark_meaning.about: Asked first, once per selected shape (at most MAX_MARK_MEANING_QUESTIONS), before any other question. The AI never assumes what a selected mark means; the sketcher says. The AI writes the question and the first two options, its best reading and the next most likely one. The third option is fixed and lets the sketcher type their own words. The answer is what the sketcher saw the marks as, and it wins over the AI's own reading (design doc, item 17).
